subject: APAC microregion resourcing ask — Singapore vs Tokyo pilot sizing
messages:
From: Hiroshi Tanaka <hiroshi.t@taikocloud.jp>
To: rohan.mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: alex.mercer@cloudinfra.io
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 03:18:00 +0000
Subject: Initial ask — APAC pilot sizing and residency constraints

Rohan,

Thanks again for the intro call earlier — TaikoCloud is excited to test Redwood Dedicated for our latency-sensitive inference workloads in Asia. We attached a rough traffic estimate and a short SOW draft for the pilot.

Two asks up front:
- We need a recommended pilot pool size for Singapore (primary) and a Tokyo fallback (secondary) — this pilot is for a PoC that will run 24/7 for 8 weeks.
- Can you confirm whether KMS-backed keying and customer-managed audit logs are available in the private deployment for Singapore? Our compliance team flagged data residency + key control as blockers.

Looking for rough numbers (node counts, expected sustained tokens/sec) and any lead times. We have a target start window of mid-May.

Attachments: Taiko_traffic_estimate.xlsx, Regional_Onramp_SOW_v1.pdf

Best,
Hiroshi Tanaka
Head of ML Ops, TaikoCloud
hiroshi.t@taikocloud.jp
+81 3-1234-5678
From: rohan.mehta@redwood.ai
To: Hiroshi Tanaka <hiroshi.t@taikocloud.jp>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial ask — APAC pilot sizing and residency constraints

Hi Hiroshi — thanks for the packet and the timeline. Looping in Irene (infrastructure/ops) and Monica (commercial) to scope the pilot and compliance checks.

Preliminary response:
- Pilot sizing: based on the traffic matrix in the spreadsheet (peak ~18k rps inference bursts, average sustained ~3k rps), I propose a conservative pilot of 8 GPU nodes (A100-class equivalent) colocated in Singapore with headroom for brief bursts. That aligns to ~80 concurrent sessions with 512-token median context and expected 1.2k tokens/sec sustained across the pool. If you want headroom for heavier batch requests we can push to 12 nodes.
- Fallback: Tokyo can be set up as a warm-fallback region with 4 nodes held in reserve and automated routing on regional failures; failover SLO would be best-effort 99.5%.
- Lead time: Singapore provisioning for Dedicated typically 4–6 weeks for new accounts in a greenfield region. If we reuse existing partner racks we can compress to ~2–3 weeks but that requires market access and procurement alignment.
- KMS/audit: short answer — yes, customer-managed KMS and audit log forwarding possible in Private deployments; need legal + security to sign off on key rotation practices.

Irene/Monica — can you confirm infra lead times and whether we can pre-reserve the 8-node pilot quota for mid-May? Monica, I expect there will be a short SOW and a small MRR commit for the reserved pilot.

Rohan
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: rohan.mehta@redwood.ai, Hiroshi Tanaka <hiroshi.t@taikocloud.jp>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 01:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial ask — APAC pilot sizing and residency constraints

Hi Hiroshi — quick infra note from my side:

Operational considerations:
- Singapore availability: we have partner capacity at two colo providers (SG1 and SG2). SG1 gives lower-latency paths but has a 3–4 week procurement lead for reserved nodes; SG2 can be turned up in 10–14 business days but has slightly higher egress latency to certain zones.
- Node type: recommend qA100 (quantized A100) for the pilot to reduce overhead and speed kernel warmup; performance delta vs full A100 is ~10–15% but cost savings are material.
- Networking: we can front the pool with a localized edge ingress and a VPC peering path for Taiko's traffic. For key control, we'll integrate with Taiko's KMS via cross-account role; legal will need to verify key custody language.
- Failover plan: Tokyo warm reserve (4 nodes) + cross-region prefix caching for 90s cold-start mitigation. We can do canary traffic routing over 15–30 minute windows.

Action items for provisioning:
1) Monica to confirm SOW terms + deposit by 2027-04-21 to hold SG2 slots.
2) Taiko to provide final traffic profile (per-endpoint RPS by hour) and any inbound IP allowlist.
3) Legal thread for KMS wording (Taiko Legal + Redwood Legal).

I will start an infra ticket for resource reservation once Monica confirms commitment.

-Irene
Infrastructure Ops, Redwood Inference
From: monica.patel@redwood.ai
To: rohan.mehta@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: Hiroshi Tanaka <hiroshi.t@taikocloud.jp>, Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cloudinfra.io>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:33:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial ask — APAC pilot sizing and residency constraints

Hiroshi — thanks for the estimate. Commercials and quick SOW notes below.

SOW summary (pilot):
- Duration: 8 weeks
- Reserved capacity: 8 qA100 nodes (Singapore primary), 4 qA100 nodes (Tokyo warm reserve)
- Commitment: 8-week pilot fee equal to 40% of our monthly dedicated unit price to reserve nodes + standard overage billing.
- Deliverables: infra provisioning, onboarding runbook, 24/7 escalation channel during pilot, 2 performance reviews (week 2 and week 6).

Next steps:
- If Taiko signs the attached SOW and returns the deposit by 2027-04-21, we will prioritize SG2 partner rack and aim for provisioning start on 2027-05-05.
- We will put a soft hold on the SG2 slots pending deposit (hold expires 2027-04-24).

Alex (CloudInfra) — if you can confirm partner rack availability for SG2 we can finalize the start window.

Monica Patel
Customer Success / Commercials, Redwood Inference
From: Hiroshi Tanaka <hiroshi.t@taikocloud.jp>
To: monica.patel@redwood.ai, rohan.mehta@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@taikocloud.jp
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 16:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial ask — APAC pilot sizing and residency constraints

Monica / Rohan / Irene — thanks, this looks workable. We will sign the pilot SOW and wire the deposit by EOD 2027-04-21 to lock SG2. A couple of quick clarifications before we sign: 

1) Can you confirm the monitoring hooks we will get (token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, and KV cache hit rates)? We need these metrics for our CSM.
2) For KMS, Taiko requires that keys remain in our KMS and that Redwood only have a rollover-service role (no export). Is that achievable for the Singapore private deployment?

We will send the final traffic breakdown tomorrow and will loop legal on the KMS clause.

Regards,
Hiroshi

>
> Rohan
